🔗 Save $6,000 A Year with My Complete Amish Home-Saving Method I teach:
https://eliasyoder.com

Cheese seems like one of those things that must come from a factory. It sits there in the cold case at the store, wrapped in plastic, and most folks have no notion at all how it is made, or that it could be made, by their own hands, in their own kitchen, out of nothing but a pot of milk. They believe cheese is a mystery, a thing made by machines in some far-off plant, beyond the reach of an ordinary person. And I am going to show you how wrong that is.
Because you can make a fine, firm, delicious cheese at home, in about an hour of actual work, out of nothing but a pot of milk, a couple of eggs, and a spoonful of sour cream. No special cultures, no rennet, no cheesemaking kit, no machine. Just milk and a couple of things you already have, and a sieve, and a little patience.
Now let me be straight with you, as I always am, about what this is. This is a fresh cheese, a young cheese, the kind the old farm wives made fresh and ate fresh, firm and mild and lovely. It is not an aged sharp cheddar or a cheese cured for months in a cave, those are their own long art. But this fresh farmer's cheese is one of the most useful cheeses there is, wonderful sliced on bread, crumbled into cooking, fried, or eaten just as it is, and you can make it any day you please for a fraction of what the store charges.
